functions.label: main: read + call parser + DONE line
functions.role: reads up to 1 MiB from stdin, calls the parser, prints "DONE <count>"

functions.label: frame parser
functions.role: core: walks the stream; at offset o requires p[o] == 0xAA, else prints "ERR <o> sync" and stops; needs 3 header bytes and len <= 64 ("ERR <o> trunc"); check byte chk = (cmd*7 + len*3 + sum(p[o+3+i]*(i+1))) & 0xFF must equal the trailing byte ("ERR <o> chk"); prints "OK cmd=%02x len=%d chk=%02x" per good frame

algorithm: Frame format 0xAA <cmd> <len> <payload[len]> <chk> with len <= 64 and chk = (cmd*7 + len*3 + sum(payload[i]*(i+1))) & 0xFF. The parser emits one verdict line per frame (OK/ERR with the failing offset and reason: sync/trunc/chk) and stops at the first bad frame; after the loop main prints "DONE <n>" with the count of valid frames. All of this is visible directly in the decompile at 0x101190: the (uVar8 + 4 + uVar9) stride (3 header + len + 1 check byte), the bVar2*8 - bVar2 product (cmd*7), and the weighted payload sum (byte * loop index).
